title: Heap Sort
description: Sort in place with guaranteed O(n log n) time by building a max-heap and repeatedly moving the root to the end.

data.text: Sort an array in ascending order using heap sort: build a max-heap in place, then repeatedly swap the maximum to the end of the unsorted region and restore the heap property. The time must be O(n log n) in the worst case, and it must use O(1) extra memory.

A complete binary tree can be stored directly in an array with no pointers: for index `i`, the children are at `2i + 1` and `2i + 2`, and the parent is at `(i - 1) / 2`. That is what makes heap sort in-place. A max-heap has every parent at least as large as its children, so the root is the overall maximum.
The core operation: if a node is smaller than one of its children, swap it with the larger child and continue. This 'sinks' a misplaced value to its correct level in O(log n).

data.title: Sift down O(log n)
data.content: Swap with the larger child until the heap property holds.

data.text: Step 2: Build the Heap, Then Extract

Sift down from the last parent to the root to build a max-heap in O(n) — not O(n log n), because most nodes sit near the bottom and can only sink a little. Then repeatedly swap the root to the end and shrink the heap by one, sifting down each time.

data.title: Heap sort O(n log n), O(1) extra space
data.content: Build, then extract the maximum into the growing sorted suffix.

data.title: Building the heap is linear, not n log n
data.text: Starting from `n/2 - 1` skips all the leaves, which are trivially valid heaps. The total work is bounded by the sum of the heights of the internal nodes, which converges to O(n). Getting this wrong (sifting down from every index) still sorts correctly but loses the linear build.

data.title: Why not use heap sort everywhere?
data.text: Heap sort has the best worst-case guarantee and O(1) space, but it jumps around the array, so it loses badly on cache locality. In practice merge sort and quick sort are several times faster. Heap sort's real job is as the safety net inside introsort.

data.caption: Each extraction swaps the heap root (the maximum) to the end of the array and shrinks the heap by one.

data.title: Complete solution
data.content: Heap sort is the answer to 'which sort guarantees O(n log n) with O(1) space' — merge sort needs linear memory and quick sort has a quadratic worst case. Interviewers ask it to check that you know the trade-off triangle between time, space, and stability.
